name: walkthrough
title: Building a Bytecode VM for Mini
description: Walk through the complete implementation from bytecode inspection to a working VM with compiler, optimizations, and performance comparison.

steps.description: Import the dis module to inspect Python bytecode
Define a simple add function
Disassemble the add function to see its bytecode

steps.question: What is the first bytecode instruction for add?

steps.description: Move to opcode definitions
Import IntEnum and auto for opcode enumeration
Define stack manipulation opcodes: PUSH_INT, PUSH_FLOAT, PUSH_STR, PUSH_BOOL, PUSH_NIL, POP, DUP, SWAP
Define arithmetic opcodes: ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, NEG, POW
Move to instruction and chunk definitions
Import dataclasses and typing for instruction and chunk definitions
Define Instruction dataclass with opcode and operand
Define Chunk dataclass with emit, patch, and length methods

steps.question: How many instructions are in the test chunk?

steps.description: Move to hand-compiled expression example
Define Num, Bool, Str, Nil classes for literal values
Define Name and Assign classes for variable handling
Define BinOp and UnaryOp classes for arithmetic and logic operations
Move to compiler class
Re-define Opcode, Instruction, and Chunk for the compiler
Compile literal values: Num, Bool, Str, Nil
Compile binary operations with operand compilation in post-order
Print bytecode for the if-else example
Move to patch-back technique explanation
Re-define all components for the VM: Opcode, Instruction, Chunk
Define VM class with stack, frames, and globals
Move to full pipeline integration
Define complete Opcode, Instruction, Chunk, AST classes, and compile_and_run function
Define compile_and_run glue function that compiles and executes
Define fib program with recursive calls
Move to performance comparison
Import time module for benchmarking
Define TreeWalker interpreter as reference implementation
Define Compiler2 that compiles AST to bytecode
Define VM2 that executes bytecode

steps.question: What is fib(22) for both implementations?

steps.description: Move to upvalue pattern for closures
Define LOAD_UPVALUE and STORE_UPVALUE opcodes
Define Upvalue class with cell, is_open, value property, close method

steps.question: What is the upvalue state after close?

steps.description: Move to closure factory example
Define opcodes including MAKE_CLOSURE
Define MiniClosure to simulate VM closures
Define make_counter_vm that creates closure with shared cell

steps.question: What does the first counter call return?

steps.description: Move to disassembler
Define disassemble function to pretty-print bytecode
Build fib chunk by hand with STORE_LOCAL, LOAD_LOCAL, PUSH_INT, LE, JUMP_IF_FALSE, SUB, CALL, ADD, RETURN
Disassemble the fib chunk
Move to compile_and_run pipeline
Define complete set of classes and compile_and_run function
Define end-to-end test with while loop summing 1 through 5
Compile and run the while loop program
Move to performance comparison with tree-walker
Define TreeWalker class for reference interpreter
Define Compiler2 with minimal instruction set
Define VM2 with minimal opcode support
Time both implementations on fib(22) and report speedup
Move to optimization introduction
Define example showing valid and invalid optimizations
Move to constant folding and propagation
Define AST node types for constant folding: Num, Var, BinOp, UnaryOp, Let, If
Define fold_and_propagate function with constant propagation and folding
Define pretty printer for AST nodes
Run fold_and_propagate on test cases
Move to common subexpression elimination
Define Upvalue class and CSE helper functions
Define cse, expr_key, is_pure, wrap_bindings functions
Test CSE on (x+1)*(x+1) expression

steps.question: What is the CSE result for (x+1)*(x+1)?

steps.description: Move to function inlining
Define AST types for inlining: Num, Var, BinOp, Lambda, App, Let
Define substitute function for replacing free variables
Define inline function with size limit to prevent code explosion
Move to tail call optimization
Set up to handle large factorial results
Define non-tail-recursive and tail-recursive factorial functions
Define Thunk class and trampoline function for TCO simulation
Define fact_tramp using Thunk for constant stack depth

steps.question: What are the last 5 digits of fact_tramp(5000)?
